title: Who Does What? Organizing Explained | Principles of Management Ep 16
description:
Chai Corner now has two outlets and eight people, but nobody is sure who does what. At the bus stand two people make tea and nobody washes the cups, both outlets buy milk on the same day, and every small question still goes to Ravi. In this animated lesson we use his chai stall to understand organizing and departmentation.

You will see Kabir find the problem in the books, then learn what organizing means: everyone gets a clear role, clear authority and a clear boss. We build Chai Corner's structure step by step: list the activities, group them, give each group an owner, delegate authority and link the groups. Then we cover departmentation and its five common types (functional, territorial, product, customer and process), watch Ravi mix territorial and functional departments, and see each type at work in companies, banks, vehicle makers and garment factories. We also look honestly at the catch: departments can turn into silos, and Henri Fayol's gangplank (1916) lets people on the same level talk directly across departments.

This is Episode 16 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
